QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_50

question.text: A Cat III AIF adopts GIPS standards. The fund is 3 years old. What is the minimum GIPS-compliant performance period it must report, and how does this evolve?

answer.text: 5 years or since-inception (whichever shorter), adding one year each year up to a 10-year minimum after which it rolls

explanation.text: The Logic: Per GIPS, funds must present a minimum of 5 years (or since inception if younger) of annual performance, adding one year each subsequent year, reaching a 10-year minimum thereafter. For our 3-year fund, they would report since-inception. The Trap: A/C/D each misstate the GIPS evolution rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C All-Cat Manager tests GIPS. XIX-E tests Cat III application — especially reporting composites by strategy. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document your GIPS compliance procedure with an independent verifier (e.g., ACA Compliance, KPMG). LPs from institutional pools (sovereign wealth, pension funds) MANDATE verified GIPS compliance for their allocation process.
